title: Your 401(k)'s biggest bet just doubled

lines: Nvidia's revenue in a single quarter — up 103% from a year ago.
That's roughly double what it earned a year earlier.
Net income alone: $65.3 billion in three months.
Nvidia is about 8% of the S&P 500 — the biggest single holding in most 401(k)s and index funds.

Is Nvidia your biggest holding without you choosing it?

source_line: Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 release (SEC filing), Nov. 17, 2026
caption:
Nvidia just doubled its revenue in three months — and it might be the biggest bet in your 401(k).

The chipmaker reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the quarter that ended Oct. 25, up 103% from a year ago. Net income was $65.3 billion, and its AI data-center sales jumped 110%.

Here's why it matters even if you've never bought a share: Nvidia is the world's most valuable company and about 8% of the S&P 500 — the single largest holding in most index funds and target-date retirement accounts.

This was also its first report since founder Jensen Huang stepped down, with former CFO Colette Kress now interim CEO. Shares rose after hours.

My take: one company now moves the fund millions of people retire on — however good the quarter, that's a lot riding on one stock.
